title: It’s Getting Hot, Hot, Hot!
author: Tom Engelhardt
content:
[![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/immo-wegmann-
qs5HR1dG7h4-unsplash-680x481.jpg)](https://www.counterpunch.org/2026/07/22/its-
getting-hot-hot-hot/)

![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/immo-wegmann-
qs5HR1dG7h4-unsplash-680x481.jpg)

Image by Immo Wegmann.

Before I truly begin, let me say one thing: It’s eternally unnerving to find
myself writing so often about “our” president and so facing the fact (yet
again!) that the American people elected such a man not just once but twice --
someone mad enough to put significant effort into quite literally trying to
destroy our planet (at least as we’ve known it).

Let’s face it: Donald Trump should be considered an atomic bomb of a president
(potentially all too literally, even if in slow motion, thanks to climate
change). When it comes to actual atomic weaponry, he’s been threatening for a
while first to
[restart](https://substack.com/redirect/b8c52f6b-cebc-46d0-81a2-6d030929063b?j=eyJ1IjoiY3hzYyJ9.fFDCZd86HpEg4wUdrRqIBWFdQUxLbjfFhZT671sU_AQ)
the testing of nuclear weapons, which the U.S. stopped 33 years ago, and then
(at least implicitly) to use just such a weapon against the Iranians. In
April, in fact, he
[insisted](https://substack.com/redirect/945465f0-961a-4611-9cf6-2070dfb94643?j=eyJ1IjoiY3hzYyJ9.fFDCZd86HpEg4wUdrRqIBWFdQUxLbjfFhZT671sU_AQ)
that, if Iran refused to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, “[a whole
civilization](https://substack.com/redirect/dabc87aa-d6a1-483b-a9af-f472875721a6?j=eyJ1IjoiY3hzYyJ9.fFDCZd86HpEg4wUdrRqIBWFdQUxLbjfFhZT671sU_AQ)
will die tonight, never to be brought back” -- only to later deny that he
meant he would ever consider using an atomic weapon against that country.

Of course, once upon a time in school (think the 1950s), the young Donald
Trump, like me, must have “[ducked and
covered](https://substack.com/redirect/5cac473e-cccd-46eb-9aea-677a06332d83?j=eyJ1IjoiY3hzYyJ9.fFDCZd86HpEg4wUdrRqIBWFdQUxLbjfFhZT671sU_AQ)“
under his desk in preparation for a potential Soviet atomic attack on our city
(New York). During those Cold War years, of course, atomic testing was
considered normal, while our country and the Soviet Union were indeed facing
off globally in a remarkably threatening fashion. But no ducking and covering
now, not from our president anyway.

Once upon a time, in the last century when I was an editor at Pantheon Books,
I published  _[Unforgettable Fire: Pictures Drawn by Atomic Bomb
Survivors](https://substack.com/redirect/4c673a1a-6f24-4432-b73b-fecbfd22a2cb?j=eyJ1IjoiY3hzYyJ9.fFDCZd86HpEg4wUdrRqIBWFdQUxLbjfFhZT671sU_AQ)_.
Then, at the invitation of the Japanese editor of that book, I actually
visited Hiroshima and went to the museum there dedicated to my country’s
nuclear devastation of that city and Nagasaki to end World War II. I’ll never
forget that dead [12-year-old’s charred
lunchbox](https://substack.com/redirect/c56ee278-0707-48ee-a59b-3fe4899ea9a6?j=eyJ1IjoiY3hzYyJ9.fFDCZd86HpEg4wUdrRqIBWFdQUxLbjfFhZT671sU_AQ)
or that [human
shadow](https://substack.com/redirect/28cb4c09-dd52-440e-8e49-21344b033dc9?j=eyJ1IjoiY3hzYyJ9.fFDCZd86HpEg4wUdrRqIBWFdQUxLbjfFhZT671sU_AQ)
etched in stone by the atomic blast. Of course, as a boy, I had all too
typically grown-up dreaming (in the sense of a nightmare) about mushroom
clouds exploding over New York City.

But in all those years, I never quite imagined that there might be a slow-
motion version of atomic warfare on this planet, which we’ve come to mildly
label “climate change.” (It should, of course, be called something more like
“climate catastrophe” or “climate hell.”) Nor had I ever quite imagined that
we would elect a president seemingly intent on making it happen ever more
quickly and severely. After all, he’s pushed remarkably hard to further
fossil-fuelize our world. As Juan Cole noted all too aptly at his  _[Informed
Comment](https://substack.com/redirect/855585d3-6547-4ed9-a919-342ae6ad7986?j=eyJ1IjoiY3hzYyJ9.fFDCZd86HpEg4wUdrRqIBWFdQUxLbjfFhZT671sU_AQ)_[
website](https://substack.com/redirect/855585d3-6547-4ed9-a919-342ae6ad7986?j=eyJ1IjoiY3hzYyJ9.fFDCZd86HpEg4wUdrRqIBWFdQUxLbjfFhZT671sU_AQ),
just as the 250th anniversary of this country’s founding was passing, “Trump’s
promotion of coal burning and cancellation of wind turbines makes him the
Benedict Arnold of America’s current struggle.”

These days, of course, [nine
countries](https://substack.com/redirect/7572c33e-c203-46dd-a7f3-9b106540b7c8?j=eyJ1IjoiY3hzYyJ9.fFDCZd86HpEg4wUdrRqIBWFdQUxLbjfFhZT671sU_AQ)
have nuclear arsenals (enough weapons to wipe out any number of Earth-sized
planets), and Donald Trump has recently been at war with Iran, the country he
feared might become the tenth. And yet, in the 80 years since my country ended
World War II by dropping atomic bombs on the Japanese cities of Hiroshima and
Nagasaki, killing [more than 200,000
people](https://substack.com/redirect/8cf88f9c-16f1-4dcb-
bc9c-df2e30638c39?j=eyJ1IjoiY3hzYyJ9.fFDCZd86HpEg4wUdrRqIBWFdQUxLbjfFhZT671sU_AQ)
(including an estimated 38,000 children), consider it a miracle that another
of those weapons (now horrifically more powerful) has never been used,
although since the first nuclear test in 1945, there have been more than
[2,000](https://substack.com/redirect/1cae0c63-923d-4850-b611-98fb7c8aa1a7?j=eyJ1IjoiY3hzYyJ9.fFDCZd86HpEg4wUdrRqIBWFdQUxLbjfFhZT671sU_AQ)
other “tests” in which such weapons were exploded, which have, of course, sent
[cancer-causing
radiation](https://substack.com/redirect/075bfd79-1911-4530-831b-6862553bafd8?j=eyJ1IjoiY3hzYyJ9.fFDCZd86HpEg4wUdrRqIBWFdQUxLbjfFhZT671sU_AQ)
across the planet.

But don’t push that miracle idea too far, since it turns out that we humans
proved all too capable of coming up with another way to devastate this planet,
a distinctly slow-motion version of atomic warfare. In fact, at this very
moment, I’m sitting in an air-conditioned room writing this piece, while the
world more or less burns outside my window. Recently, high temperature records
were [tied or
broken](https://substack.com/redirect/a5ad114b-a3f5-47a8-9242-a784d57432eb?j=eyJ1IjoiY3hzYyJ9.fFDCZd86HpEg4wUdrRqIBWFdQUxLbjfFhZT671sU_AQ)
across 21 states in my country, including my own state, with worse potentially
still to come in our future. (The same, by the way, has been true [across much
of Europe](https://substack.com/redirect/2cc572af-
bce4-4346-b20e-ad7a2e40753e?j=eyJ1IjoiY3hzYyJ9.fFDCZd86HpEg4wUdrRqIBWFdQUxLbjfFhZT671sU_AQ),
the part of the planet [reputedly heating
fastest](https://substack.com/redirect/b8c2d81a-8675-4c60-8de1-972030aae824?j=eyJ1IjoiY3hzYyJ9.fFDCZd86HpEg4wUdrRqIBWFdQUxLbjfFhZT671sU_AQ)
in this increasingly strange world of ours, with Spain only recently [topping
a record 113
degrees](https://substack.com/redirect/e18ce6bb-a5eb-494c-ada5-e2ccf3d72a1d?j=eyJ1IjoiY3hzYyJ9.fFDCZd86HpEg4wUdrRqIBWFdQUxLbjfFhZT671sU_AQ)
Fahrenheit.) I’m thinking, of course, of climate change and, sadly, at this
very moment, when it comes to that version of warfare -- and it should indeed
be thought of as a form of warfare! -- against this planet, there really is no
ducking and covering (unless you count [air
conditioning](https://substack.com/redirect/89508c1a-e8cf-43a0-bd1a-8442407a96ae?j=eyJ1IjoiY3hzYyJ9.fFDCZd86HpEg4wUdrRqIBWFdQUxLbjfFhZT671sU_AQ),
which uses electricity and so only makes matters worse). If you happened to
live in Europe recently or in the midwestern and eastern parts of the United
States where temperatures [rose
to](https://substack.com/redirect/d759c1f8-79c8-45ae-8e97-b33fc0e4cf01?j=eyJ1IjoiY3hzYyJ9.fFDCZd86HpEg4wUdrRqIBWFdQUxLbjfFhZT671sU_AQ)
striking heights or simply went crazy ([including hitting 104
degrees](https://substack.com/redirect/a5ad114b-a3f5-47a8-9242-a784d57432eb?j=eyJ1IjoiY3hzYyJ9.fFDCZd86HpEg4wUdrRqIBWFdQUxLbjfFhZT671sU_AQ)
in my hometown, New York City), you would certainly know that.

In short, it’s increasingly hot, hot, hot, damagingly so on this planet of
ours, and Donald Trump, the second time around, not only doesn’t give a damn
(an all too appropriate term under the circumstances) but seems remarkably
intent on making this planet hotter still. At least, to look on the bright
side, climate change did [make something of a
mess](https://substack.com/redirect/3731ae01-169a-46c2-aa46-dacb98fc516d?j=eyJ1IjoiY3hzYyJ9.fFDCZd86HpEg4wUdrRqIBWFdQUxLbjfFhZT671sU_AQ)
of his celebration of the 250th anniversary of American independence, or was
that the 250th anniversary of Glorious Donald? When it comes to him and the
possibility of either a potentially devastating nuclear war or a fossil-
fuelized heat war on this planet, he seems perfectly willing to engage in
world-ending activities as long as they’re in slow motion and, at 80 years
old, he (like me) won’t be around to experience the resulting holocaust, which
he has, of course,
[termed](https://substack.com/redirect/4dc35695-d63e-40c6-9abf-a0daf9db2df0?j=eyJ1IjoiY3hzYyJ9.fFDCZd86HpEg4wUdrRqIBWFdQUxLbjfFhZT671sU_AQ)
a “green energy scam” and a “hoax.”

Yes, make no mistake about it, while he’s [officially
ended](https://substack.com/redirect/295d4d4f-ecd9-498a-a865-bd1441af9f74?j=eyJ1IjoiY3hzYyJ9.fFDCZd86HpEg4wUdrRqIBWFdQUxLbjfFhZT671sU_AQ)
that 33-year moratorium on nuclear testing, that may be the least of our
problems. Whatever other recent presidents have (or haven’t) done in terms of
climate change, he seems remarkably intent on doing so much worse by [wildly
promoting fossil
fuels](https://substack.com/redirect/b889fbf1-3cd4-400d-8c64-ea5b4344985d?j=eyJ1IjoiY3hzYyJ9.fFDCZd86HpEg4wUdrRqIBWFdQUxLbjfFhZT671sU_AQ),
while doing everything he can to dismiss anything that might make this planet
less hot, including
[wind](https://substack.com/redirect/99164137-03f7-448d-9404-77673d002e28?j=eyJ1IjoiY3hzYyJ9.fFDCZd86HpEg4wUdrRqIBWFdQUxLbjfFhZT671sU_AQ)
and
[solar](https://substack.com/redirect/eece35a2-4f75-42d2-9e76-41e50427584d?j=eyJ1IjoiY3hzYyJ9.fFDCZd86HpEg4wUdrRqIBWFdQUxLbjfFhZT671sU_AQ)
power of any sort. (In the process, he’s giving imperial decline a new meaning
by turning what’s left of imperial power on this planet over to China, which
now [controls](https://substack.com/redirect/e4b71906-a3c5-4112-9fda-
dc652e7ca170?j=eyJ1IjoiY3hzYyJ9.fFDCZd86HpEg4wUdrRqIBWFdQUxLbjfFhZT671sU_AQ)
so much of green energy development and production.)

If his dreams (oh, sorry, nightmares) come true, he will certainly be known
historically (if, of course, there is any “historically” then) as the
president of the United States who did his best to end it all (even if in slow
motion).

Under the circumstances, we should consider Donald Trump the human equivalent
of a slow-motion atomic bomb.

[Substack](https://tomengelhardt.substack.com/p/its-getting-hot-hot-hot)._
